summary.whatChanges: The `accepts` helper now compares Accept-style header values case-insensitively, lowercasing both the client's accept entry and the supported entry (including wildcard subtype matching) before comparison. The returned value still uses the caller's original `supports` casing. Tests cover media types, language tags, wildcards, and q=0 entries.
behaviorChanges: Requests with `Accept: TEXT/HTML` now match a supported `text/html` instead of falling back to the default
Case-different subtype wildcards like `TEXT/*` now match `text/html`
A case-different entry with `q=0` (e.g. `EN;q=0`) is now correctly treated as not acceptable, yielding the default
risks: Applications that relied on exact case matching to reject differently-cased Accept values will now match and may select a different response type or language
Lowercasing happens on every comparison call, adding minor per-request allocation in the negotiation loop
Only `matchType` is case-folded; any other casing-sensitive logic in the parse/sort path (e.g. q-value handling elsewhere) is unchanged and could remain inconsistent
